Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: Hi, I'm Virginia. I'm here because I hurt my knee playing basketball. I was playing with Jerry, and he ran into me, and I fell to the ground. My knee has been hurting on the inside ever since, and it's still swollen. I had ice and an ace wrap, but I can't really put weight on it.
Doctor: Can you describe the exact location of the pain on your knee and whether it radiates to other areas? Have you experienced any locking, clicking, or giving way of the knee since the injury?
Patient: The pain is on the inside of my knee, right where it's swollen. It doesn't radiate anywhere else. I haven't had any locking or clicking, but it does feel unstable sometimes, like it might give way if I try to put too much weight on it.
Doctor: Have you had any prior knee injuries, surgeries, or episodes of instability in the same or opposite knee?
Patient: No, I haven't had any prior knee injuries or surgeries. This is the first time I've had an issue with my knee like this.
Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies or evaluations for this knee injury, such as X-rays, MRI, or a physical examination by a healthcare provider?
Patient: I haven't had any imaging studies done for this injury yet, but I did have an X-ray when I first came in. The doctor mentioned that there was some swelling and fluid in the knee, but no fractures were seen. I haven't had an MRI or any other tests done so far.
Doctor: Could you please describe the mechanism of the basketball injury in more detail, such as how the collision with Jerry occurred and whether you twisted your knee or landed awkwardly during the fall?
Patient: I was playing basketball, and Jerry ran into me. I think I twisted my knee a little before I fell to the ground on my side. I didn't land directly on my knee, but it still hurt a lot, and I couldn't get back up right away.
Doctor: Have you undergone an MRI or any other imaging studies to evaluate for ligamentous or meniscal injuries?
Patient: No, I haven't had an MRI or any other imaging studies to evaluate for ligamentous or meniscal injuries yet. The only thing they did was an X-ray when I first came in, and they said there were no fractures, just some swelling and fluid in the knee.
